Foreign guests' seasons in Europe¶

Key findings¶

  • Volume. Foreign guests spend 1.47 bn nights a year in tourist accommodation, 47% of all; 10 regions hold 36% of them. → 1
  • Season. Europe's year peaks in August (1.9× an average day). Coastal regions are the most seasonal; the capital is the least seasonal region in 18 of 26 countries. → 2
  • Foreign vs domestic. Foreign demand is more seasonal than domestic demand in 176 of 257 regions. → 2
  • Patterns. Foreign guests follow a summer season in 181 regions, winter + summer seasons in 11 (mountains) and a winter season in 3 (a small group); 64, mostly cities, are year-round. → 3
  • Effect. Today's foreign timing sharpens the season in 125 regions and smooths it in 49, but even 50% more foreign nights would move the typical region's Gini by only +0.003. → 4

Data¶

  • Eurostat tour_occ_nin2m: nights in hotels, holiday and short-stay accommodation and campsites (NACE 55.1–55.3) for the 34 countries in the extract (EU-27, EFTA, North Macedonia, Albania and Serbia) and their NUTS-2 regions (Eurostat's statistical regions, 268 here). Population and area: Eurostat demo_r_pjanaggr3 and reg_area3.
  • Every figure is the 2023–2024 average; seasonality is measured on nights per day, so month length does not count. A few series have only one usable year (Appendix).
  • Formulas, thresholds and robustness checks: Stage 2 Indices.

# Colours, chart style, maps
INK, MUTED, GRIDC = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df"
COLOR = {"Domestic": "#2a78d6", "Foreign": "#eb6834", "Total": "#1baf7a"}

def style(ax, title, ylabel=None):
    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=12)
    if ylabel:
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, color=MUTED)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines[["left", "bottom"]].set_color(MUTED)
    ax.tick_params(colors=MUTED)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRIDC, lw=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)


# Region outlines: Eurostat GISCO NUTS 2024 (1:20 million, ETRS89-LAEA), via Nuts2json - data/raw/geo/
def _rings(g):
    return [
        r for poly in (g["coordinates"] if g["type"] ==
                       "MultiPolygon" else [g["coordinates"]]) for r in poly
    ]


def _geom_path(g):
    verts, codes = [], []
    for ring in _rings(g):
        verts += ring + [ring[0]]
        codes += [Path.MOVETO
                  ] + [Path.LINETO] * (len(ring) - 1) + [Path.CLOSEPOLY]
    return Path(verts, codes)


def _centroid(g):
    """Centroid of the largest ring (the main land mass): where a region's circle is drawn."""
    best = None
    for ring in _rings(g):
        x, y = np.asarray(ring, float).T
        cross = x * np.roll(y, -1) - np.roll(x, -1) * y
        area = cross.sum() / 2
        if area != 0 and (best is None or abs(area) > abs(best[0])):
            best = (area, ((x + np.roll(x, -1)) * cross).sum() / (6 * area),
                    ((y + np.roll(y, -1)) * cross).sum() / (6 * area))
    return best[1], best[2]


_load = lambda f: json.load(open(f"data/raw/geo/{f}", encoding="utf-8"))[

MAP_CENTROID = {f["properties"]["id"]: _centroid(f["geometry"]) for f in _feat}
MAP_LAND = [_geom_path(f["geometry"]) for f in _load("cntrg.json")]
MAP_BORDERS = [
    line for f in _load("nutsbn_0.json") if f["properties"].get("co") == "F"
    for line in (f["geometry"]["coordinates"] if f["geometry"]["type"] ==

]

def magma(n, reverse=True):
    """n colours from magma without its near-black and near-white ends; reverse=True: darker = higher class."""
    cm = plt.cm.magma_r if reverse else plt.cm.magma
    return [
        matplotlib.colors.to_hex(c) for c in cm(
            np.linspace(0.12, 0.85, n) if reverse else np.
            linspace(0.15, 0.88, n))
    ]


def _draw(ax, colors, base=NODATA):
    ax.add_collection(
        PathCollection(MAP_LAND,
                       facecolor="#f1f1ef",
                       edgecolor="white",
                       lw=0.3,
                       zorder=1))
    ids = list(MAP_REGIONS)
    ax.add_collection(
        PathCollection([MAP_REGIONS[i] for i in ids],
                       facecolor=[
                           colors.get(i, base if i in REG.index else "#f1f1ef")
                           for i in ids
                       ],
                       edgecolor="white",
                       lw=0.25,
                       zorder=2))
    ax.add_collection(
        LineCollection(MAP_BORDERS, colors="white", lw=0.9, zorder=3))
    ax.set_xlim(1.85e6, 6.6e6)
    ax.set_ylim(0.9e6, 5.45e6)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.axis("off")


def _off_map(codes):
    off = sorted(set(codes) - set(MAP_REGIONS))
    if off:
        print(
            f"not on the maps (Azores, Madeira, French overseas regions): {off}"
        )


def region_map(colors, legend, title, note=None):
    """One choropleth of NUTS-2 regions. colors: NUTSCode -> colour; legend: list of (label, colour). Grey = no data."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 8.2), dpi=110)
    _draw(ax, colors)
    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=11)
    ax.legend(handles=[
        Patch(facecolor=c, edgecolor="none", label=l) for l, c in legend
    ] + [Patch(facecolor=NODATA, edgecolor="none", label="no data")],
              frameon=False,
              fontsize=8,
              loc="upper right",
              title=note,
              title_fontsize=8,
              alignment="left")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    _off_map(colors)


def _row_figure(n, title, legend, note, nodata=True):
    """Figure with n maps in a row and one legend below; returns the bottom margin the legend needs."""
    handles = [
        Patch(facecolor=c, edgecolor="none", label=l) for l, c in legend
    ] + ([Patch(facecolor=NODATA, edgecolor="none", label="no data")]
         if nodata else [])
    ncol = min(len(handles), 6)
    rows = -(-len(handles) // ncol)
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1,
                            n,
                            figsize=(5.6 * n, 6.0 + 0.25 * rows),
                            dpi=110)
    fig.suptitle(title, x=0.01, ha="left", color=INK, fontsize=12)
    fig.legend(handles=handles,
               loc="lower center",
               ncol=ncol,
               frameon=False,
               fontsize=8,
               title=note,
               title_fontsize=8)
    return fig, np.atleast_1d(axs), 0.05 + 0.035 * rows


def map_row(panels, legend, title, note, nodata=True):
    """Category maps side by side with one legend. panels: list of (subtitle, {NUTSCode: colour})."""
    fig, axs, bottom = _row_figure(len(panels), title, legend, note, nodata)
    shown = set()
    for ax, (sub, cols) in zip(axs, panels):
        _draw(ax, cols)
        ax.set_title(sub, loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=10)
        shown |= set(cols)
    plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, bottom, 1, 0.95))
    plt.show()
    _off_map(shown)


def binned_row(series, cuts, labels, title, note, reverse=True):
    """Maps side by side (dict subtitle -> Series) on one shared scale, then the number of regions in each class."""
    cols = magma(len(labels), reverse)
    fig, axs, bottom = _row_figure(len(series), title, list(zip(labels, cols)),
                                   note)
    counts, shown = {}, set()
    for ax, (sub, s) in zip(axs, series.items()):
        cls = pd.cut(s.dropna(), cuts, labels=labels, right=False)
        _draw(ax, {k: cols[labels.index(v)] for k, v in cls.items()})
        ax.set_title(sub, loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=10)
        counts[sub] = cls.value_counts().reindex(labels)
        shown |= set(cls.index)
    plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, bottom, 1, 0.95))
    plt.show()
    _off_map(shown)
    cnt = pd.DataFrame(counts).fillna(0)
    fig2, axs2 = plt.subplots(1, len(series), figsize=(5.6 * len(series), 0.3 * len(labels) + 1.3), dpi=110, sharex=True)
    y0 = np.arange(len(labels))[::-1]
    for ax2, sub in zip(np.atleast_1d(axs2), series):
        ax2.barh(y0, cnt[sub], color=cols, height=0.7)
        for y_, v in zip(y0, cnt[sub]):
            ax2.text(v + 0.5, y_, f"{v:.0f}", va="center", fontsize=8, color=MUTED)
        ax2.set_yticks(y0, labels)
        style(ax2, f"{sub}: regions by class")
        ax2.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
        ax2.grid(axis="x", color=GRIDC, lw=0.8)
        ax2.set_xlabel("NUTS-2 regions", color=MUTED)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def top_table(series, fmt):
    """Top 10 regions of each series (dict subtitle -> Series), side by side."""
    out = {}
    for sub, s in series.items():
        t = s.dropna().nlargest(10)
        out[sub] = [
            f"{REG.at[k, 'Region'][:30]} ({fmt(v)})" for k, v in t.items()
        ]
    display(pd.DataFrame(out, index=pd.RangeIndex(1, 11, name="rank")))

# Usable series: 12 published months, none confidential, at least 100,000 nights a year (details in the Appendix)
MIN_NIGHTS = 100_000
complete = NPD.notna().all(axis=1)
confidential = FLAGS["C"].reindex(NPD.index, fill_value=False)
big_enough = ANNUAL.reindex(NPD.index) >= MIN_NIGHTS
USABLE = complete & ~confidential & big_enough
LOWREL = FLAGS["u"].reindex(USABLE.index, fill_value=False)[USABLE].groupby(
    level=["NUTSCode", "ResidenceCountry"]).any()
NIGHTS_AVG = ANNUAL.reindex(NPD.index)[USABLE].groupby(
    level=["NUTSCode", "ResidenceCountry"]).mean()  # average annual nights

1. Tourism volume, intensity and density¶

↑ Contents

Measures: volume, intensity and density¶

Nights spent = nights in tourist accommodation a year, average of 2023 and 2024 (Eurostat's annual totals).

Foreign share = foreign nights ÷ all nights × 100, over 2023 and 2024 together. Groups: mainly domestic under 40%, mixed 40–70%, mainly foreign 70% or more.

Tourism intensity = nights a year ÷ residents (average population of 2023 and 2024). Read: 5 = five nights in tourist accommodation for every resident, over the year. Counts only rented accommodation (no day visitors, second homes or stays with friends), so it understates the real pressure.

Tourism density = nights a year ÷ area in km². Read: 1,000 = 1,000 nights a year on every km²; ÷ 365 days ≈ 2.7 guests per km² on an average night.

EUROPE = pd.DataFrame({
    "nights (m)":
    A0.sum() / 1e6,
    "per inhabitant":
    A0.sum() / PPL.reindex(A0.index).sum(),
    "per km²":
    A0[REG.loc[A0.index, "AreaKm2"].notna()].sum() /
    REG.loc[A0.index, "AreaKm2"].sum()
})
print(
    "Europe (34 countries; per km² without Serbia, which has no published area):"
)
display(
    EUROPE.reindex(["Total", "Foreign",
                    "Domestic"]).rename(index={
                        "Total": "All guests"
                    }).round(1))

Which demand dominates: domestic or foreign?¶

FG = ["Mainly domestic", "Mixed", "Mainly foreign"]

c_ann = A0.copy()                                   # countries: average annual nights (Part 1, Measures)
c_ann.index = c_ann.index.map(REG["Country"])
c_ann["PrcForeign"] = 100 * c_ann["Foreign"] / c_ann["Total"]
print(
    f"Europe (34 countries), average 2023-2024: {c_ann['Total'].sum() / 1e6:,.0f} m nights a year, "

)

                              "PrcForeign": "foreign %"

print()
# NUTS-2 regions with a usable all-guest profile; nights = average of the usable years
s_ = ann.groupby(level="NUTSCode").sum()
reg = REG.loc[NUTS2].assign(PrcForeign=100 * s_["Foreign"] / s_["Total"])
reg["ForeignGroup"] = pd.Categorical(pd.cut(reg["PrcForeign"],
                                            [-np.inf, 40, 70, np.inf],
                                            right=False,
                                            labels=FG),
                                     categories=FG)
reg["Nights"] = NIGHTS_AVG.xs("Total",
                              level="ResidenceCountry").reindex(reg.index)
reg["ForeignNights"] = NIGHTS_AVG.xs(
    "Foreign", level="ResidenceCountry").reindex(reg.index)

grp = reg.groupby("ForeignGroup",
                  observed=False).agg(regions=("Region", "size"),
                                      all_nights=("Nights", "sum"),
                                      foreign_nights=("ForeignNights", "sum"))
grp["% of all nights"] = (100 * grp["all_nights"] /
                          grp["all_nights"].sum()).round(1)
grp["% of foreign nights"] = (100 * grp["foreign_nights"] /
                              grp["foreign_nights"].sum()).round(1)

2. How seasonal is Europe?¶

↑ Contents

Measures: seasonality¶

Gini index - how unequally the year's nights are spread over the 12 months: 0 = every month equal, 0.917 = all nights in one month. Classes: Low (no clear season) under 0.15, Medium 0.15–0.33, High 0.33 or more.

Season75 - how many of the busiest months together hold 75% of the year's nights: 9 = an even year, 3 = a three-month season. A whole number, so coarse: an easy-to-read companion of the Gini index.

Spread ratio - tells one season from two. It compares the Gini index with S_R, a measure that also counts how far apart the busy months lie on the calendar: about 1 = one season, lower = the busy months split into separate seasons (ski + summer ≈ 0.55).

Each region's year is its 2023–2024 average profile: the share of the year's nights per day in each month. Formulas: Stage 2, part B.

In [9]:
def gini(y):
    """Gini index of 12 values: 2 cov(y, rank) / (12 mean)."""
    y = np.asarray(y, float)
    r = np.empty(12)
    r[np.argsort(y, kind="stable")] = np.arange(1, 13)
    return 2 * np.mean((y - y.mean()) * (r / 12 - (r / 12).mean())) / y.mean()


def s_r(y):
    """S_R: least effort to flatten the year, months on a circle."""
    y = np.asarray(y, float)
    d = np.cumsum(y - y.mean())
    return np.abs(d - np.median(d)).sum() / (3 * y.sum())


LOW, HIGH = 0.15, 0.33
GCLASS = ["Low", "Medium", "High"]
SEASONS = [
    "One season", "Main + secondary season", "Two seasons", "No clear season"
]

ok_ = NPD[USABLE.reindex(NPD.index, fill_value=False)]
PROF = ok_.div(ok_.sum(axis=1),
               axis=0).groupby(level=["NUTSCode", "ResidenceCountry"
                                      ]).mean()  # 2023-2024 profile (shares)
FAC = 12 * PROF  # seasonal factors
NPD_AVG = ok_.groupby(
    level=["NUTSCode", "ResidenceCountry"]).mean()  # average nights per day

ix = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Gini": [gini(r) for r in PROF.to_numpy()],
        "SR": [s_r(r) for r in PROF.to_numpy()],
        "PeakMonth": PROF.idxmax(axis=1)
    },
    index=PROF.index)


def season75(y):
    """Number of busiest months holding 75% of the year."""
    v = np.sort(np.asarray(y, float))[::-1]
    return int(np.argmax(np.cumsum(v) >= 0.75 * v.sum() - 1e-12)) + 1


ix["Season75"] = [season75(r) for r in PROF.to_numpy()]
ix["SpreadRatio"] = ix["SR"] / ix["Gini"]
ix["GiniClass"] = pd.Categorical(pd.cut(ix["Gini"], [0, LOW, HIGH, 1.01],
                                        right=False,
                                        labels=GCLASS),
                                 categories=GCLASS)
ix["SeasonCount"] = pd.Categorical(np.select(
    [ix["Gini"] < LOW, ix["SpreadRatio"] >= 0.9, ix["SpreadRatio"] >= 0.6],
    ["No clear season", "One season", "Main + secondary season"],
    "Two seasons"),
                                   categories=SEASONS)
ix["Nights"] = NIGHTS_AVG
ix["LowReliability"] = LOWREL.reindex(ix.index).fillna(False).astype(bool)
ix = ix.join(REG, on="NUTSCode")
sel = lambda guest, level=2: ix.xs(guest, level="ResidenceCountry").loc[
    lambda x: x["NUTSLevel"] == level]
to, fo, do = sel("Total"), sel("Foreign"), sel("Domestic")
print(
    f"NUTS-2 regions with a usable 2023-2024 profile: all guests {len(to)}, foreign {len(fo)}, domestic {len(do)}"
)

NUTS-2 regions with a usable 2023-2024 profile: all guests 268, foreign 259, domestic 263

How seasonal is each region?¶

The table shows data for Europe as one destination: it adds up the nights of all 34 countries month by month and measures that single year. Because the total is weighted by nights and the largest destinations are summer destinations, it comes out more seasonal than the typical region. The typical region is the median of the regions' own Gini values. The maps show every region's Gini for all guests and foreign guests on a shared scale.

EUR = cty.groupby(level="ResidenceCountry").sum(
)  # Europe (34 countries): nights per day by month

How many months hold three quarters of the year?¶

The same picture as the Gini maps, counted in months. Darker = fewer months = more seasonal. Follows the Gini index almost exactly (Spearman ρ −0.95 to −0.96).

Which month is the busiest?¶

The busiest month of the 2023–2024 profile (nights per day). Regions with no clear season (Gini under 0.15) are shown separately: their busiest month is barely above the others and changes with small fluctuations.

In [13]:
MCOL = {
    "May": "#e7a3d6",
    "June": "#AA4499",
    "July": "#CC6677",
    "August": "#DDCC77",
    "September": "#117733",
    "October": "#999933",
    "December": "#44AA99",
    "January": "#88CCEE",
    "February": "#332288",
    "March": "#b7d5ef"
}
OTHER, NOCLEAR = "#9b9a96", "#e8e6df"
peaks, panels = {}, []
for sub, g in GROUPS2.items():
    s_ = sel(g)
    pm = s_.loc[s_["GiniClass"] != "Low", "PeakMonth"]
    low = s_.index[s_["GiniClass"] == "Low"]
    peaks[sub] = pd.concat(
        [pm.value_counts(),
         pd.Series({"no clear season": len(low)})])
    panels.append((sub, {k: MCOL.get(v, OTHER)
                         for k, v in pm.items()} | {k: NOCLEAR
                                                    for k in low}))
present = [m for m in MCOL if any(m in v.index for v in peaks.values())]
other = any(m not in MCOL and m != "no clear season" for v in peaks.values()
            for m in v.index)
map_row(panels,
        [(m, MCOL[m])
         for m in present] + ([("other months", OTHER)] if other else []) +
        [("no clear season", NOCLEAR)], "Busiest month, 2023-2024",
        "Busiest month")
display(
    pd.DataFrame(peaks).fillna(0).astype(int).sort_values(
        "All guests", ascending=False).rename_axis("busiest month (regions)"))
print("Regions whose busiest month is not July or August for at least one guest group "
      "(— = July or August; No peak = no clear season; no data = series not usable):")

nja = nja[nja.apply(lambda c: c.notna() & ~c.isin(["July", "August", "No peak"])).any(axis=1)]
display(nja.replace({"July": "—", "August": "—"}).fillna("no data").join(REG[["Region", "Country"]])

Which regions are the most seasonal?¶

The most seasonal regions are mostly coastal: 12 of the 20 with the highest Gini have most of their residents in coastal municipalities. The others are large regions with a highly seasonal coast but most residents inland. The two Albanian regions have no coastal data.

Are foreign guests more seasonal than domestic guests? Regions¶

The Gini index of foreign nights against that of domestic nights in the same region. A difference within ±0.01 (the smallest effect worth reporting, as for the timing effect below) counts as about the same.

In [16]:
cmp_n = pd.DataFrame({"G_D": do["Gini"], "G_F": fo["Gini"]}).dropna()
cmp = cmp_n.join(REG[["Region", "Country"]])
cmp["diff"] = cmp["G_F"] - cmp["G_D"]
CMP = ["Foreign more seasonal", "About the same", "Domestic more seasonal"]
CMPCOL = {
    "Foreign more seasonal": COLOR["Foreign"],
    "About the same": "#b9b8b3",
    "Domestic more seasonal": COLOR["Domestic"]
}
cmp["which"] = pd.Categorical(np.select(
    [cmp["diff"] > 0.01, cmp["diff"] < -0.01], [CMP[0], CMP[2]], CMP[1]),
                              categories=CMP)
display(cmp["which"].value_counts().reindex(CMP).rename("regions").to_frame())
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 6.2), dpi=110)
for c in CMP:
    m_ = cmp["which"] == c

Do domestic and foreign guests peak in the same months?¶

Compared only where both guest groups have a clear season (Gini 0.15 or more): in a nearly flat year the busiest month is not meaningful.

In [19]:
both_ = do.index.intersection(fo.index)
clear = both_[(do.loc[both_, "Gini"] >= LOW) & (fo.loc[both_, "Gini"] >= LOW)]

def top_months(guest):
    o = np.argsort(
        -PROF.xs(guest, level="ResidenceCountry").loc[clear].to_numpy(),
        axis=1,
        kind="stable")
    return o[:, 0], [frozenset(r[:2]) for r in o]

3. Foreign seasonal patterns¶

↑ Contents

One season or two?¶

The Gini index treats the months as an unordered set: a ski-and-summer region and a coastal region with the same busy and quiet months score the same, although the first has two short gaps and the second one long closure. The spread ratio tells them apart: Austria, with its winter and summer seasons, ranks 15th of 34 countries by Gini but 31st by S_R. The season count of every region is in the Appendix.

In [20]:

)

Austria: rank by Gini 15 of 34 - by S_R 31

What seasonal patterns do foreign guests follow?¶

Season pattern - when the year is busy, apart from how strong (Gini) and how long (Season75) the season is: Summer season (July–August above an average day), Winter + summer seasons (December–February and July–August above), Winter season (December–February only) or Year-round (no clear season, Gini under 0.15). After Ferrante, Lo Magno & De Cantis (2018). How the patterns are made and how reliable they are: Appendix.

In [21]:
PATTERNS = [
    "Summer season", "Winter + summer seasons", "Winter season", "Year-round"
]
PCOLOR = {
    "Summer season": "#eb6834",
    "Winter + summer seasons": "#2a78d6",
    "Winter season": "#6b4fbb",
    "Year-round": "#1baf7a"
}
MIN_GROUP = 5


def silhouette_values(D, labels):
    s = []
    for i in range(len(labels)):
        same = labels == labels[i]
        same[i] = False
        a = D[i, same].mean() if same.any() else 0.0
        b = min(D[i, labels == c].mean() for c in set(labels)
                if c != labels[i])
        s.append((b - a) / max(a, b))
    return np.array(s)


def name_of(c):
    if c[["December", "January", "February"]].mean() >= 1:
        return "Winter + summer seasons" if c[
            ["July", "August"]].mean() >= 1 else "Winter season"
    return "Summer season"


dev = FAC - 1
UNIT = dev.div(np.sqrt((dev**2).sum(axis=1)), axis=0)  # shape only
seasonal = ix["Gini"] >= LOW
base = [
    k for k in UNIT.index
    if k[1] == "Foreign" and REG.at[k[0], "NUTSLevel"] == 2 and seasonal[k]
]
Xb = UNIT.loc[base].to_numpy()
Zw, Db = linkage(Xb, method="ward"), squareform(pdist(Xb))
sil = {
    k: silhouette_values(Db, fcluster(Zw, k, "maxclust")).mean()
    for k in range(3, 9)
}
K_BEST = max(sil, key=sil.get)
groups = fcluster(Zw, K_BEST, "maxclust")
names_b = FAC.loc[base].groupby(groups).mean().apply(
    name_of, axis=1).reindex(groups).to_numpy()
small = [n for n in set(names_b) if (names_b == n).sum() < MIN_GROUP]
keep = ~np.isin(names_b, small)
centres = UNIT.loc[base][keep].groupby(names_b[keep]).mean()
nearest = ((UNIT[seasonal].to_numpy()[:, None, :] -
            centres.to_numpy()[None])**2).sum(axis=2).argmin(axis=1)
ix["SeasonPattern"] = pd.Categorical(pd.Series(
    centres.index[nearest],
    index=UNIT.index[seasonal]).reindex(ix.index).fillna("Year-round"),
                                     categories=PATTERNS)
# The winter + summer group is mixed: it also holds profiles whose own year is mainly a winter or mainly a summer season.
# Its members are re-named from their own profile with the same rule; a winter season under MIN_GROUP regions is kept as a small group.
mixed = ix.index[ix["SeasonPattern"] == "Winter + summer seasons"]
ix.loc[mixed, "SeasonPattern"] = FAC.loc[mixed].apply(name_of,
                                                      axis=1).to_numpy()
to, fo, do = sel("Total"), sel("Foreign"), sel("Domestic")
mv = [
    k for k in mixed if k[1] == "Foreign" and k[0] in fo.index
    and fo.at[k[0], "SeasonPattern"] != "Winter + summer seasons"
]
# patterns with fewer than MIN_GROUP foreign NUTS-2 regions: kept, drawn dashed and labelled "small group"
SMALLP = {
    p
    for p in PATTERNS if 0 < (fo["SeasonPattern"] == p).sum() < MIN_GROUP
}
plabel = lambda p, n: f"{p} ({n}{', small group' if p in SMALLP else ''})"
final_b = ix.loc[base, "SeasonPattern"].astype(str).to_numpy()
sv = silhouette_values(Db, final_b) if len(set(final_b)) > 1 else np.array(
    [np.nan])

Where both guest groups have a summer season (138 regions), the foreign season (Season75) is shorter in 77, the same length in 42 and longer in 19
  • foreign demand has one summer season in 181 regions, winter + summer seasons in 11 (the Alps, the Czech and Slovak mountains and Norway's Innlandet) and a winter season in 3, a small group (Lapland, Sofia's region and Martinique); 64 have no clear season.
  • Summer seasons differ mainly in length, which Season75 measures: three quarters of foreign nights fall in 3–5 months in 44 summer regions and in 8 months in 63.
  • Domestic and foreign guests share a shape in 73% of regions; in 41 regions only foreign guests are seasonal, in 20 regions only domestic.
  • Where both have a summer season, the foreign season is shorter in 77 of 138 regions and longer in only 19.
  • The winter season is a small, unstable group, and five regions sit close to the cut-offs between patterns (Appendix).

Is there a typical geography for each pattern?¶

For each foreign season pattern: how often the regions of each pattern are predominantly coastal, island, inland-mountain or rural (50%+ of residents), city (50%+ of residents in cities) or the capital region, against all regions. Geography shares describe where residents live, not where guests stay.

In [24]:
def ols(y, X, groups):
    """Least squares with country-clustered standard errors and p-values from t with (countries - 1) df."""
    XtX_inv = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X)
    b = XtX_inv @ X.T @ y
    u = y - X @ b
    g = pd.factorize(groups)[0]
    G, (n, k) = g.max() + 1, X.shape
    meat = sum(np.outer(X[g == i].T @ u[g == i], X[g == i].T @ u[g == i]) for i in range(G))
    se = np.sqrt(np.diag(XtX_inv @ meat @ XtX_inv) * G / (G - 1) * (n - 1) / (n - k))
    return b, se, 2 * stats.t.sf(np.abs(b / se), G - 1)


GEO_SH = ["PrcCoastal", "PrcRural", "PrcIsland", "PrcInlandMountain"]
FACTORS = ["coastal", "rural", "island", "inland mountain", "capital region"]
pg = fo.dropna(subset=GEO_SH).copy()
pg["Capital"] = pg.index.isin(list(CAPITAL.values())).astype(float)
GEO_TYPES = {
    "coastal": pg["PrcCoastal"] >= 50,
    "island": pg["PrcIsland"] >= 50,
    "inland mountain": pg["PrcInlandMountain"] >= 50,
    "rural": pg["PrcRural"] >= 50,
    "cities": pg["PrcCities"] >= 50,
    "capital region": pg["Capital"] == 1
}
shown = [p for p in PATTERNS if (pg["SeasonPattern"] == p).any()]
typ = pd.DataFrame({
    p: {
        t: 100 * m[pg["SeasonPattern"] == p].mean()
        for t, m in GEO_TYPES.items()
    }
    for p in shown
}).T
typ.loc["all regions"] = {t: 100 * m.mean() for t, m in GEO_TYPES.items()}
typ.insert(0, "regions",
           [int((pg["SeasonPattern"] == p).sum()) for p in shown] + [len(pg)])
print("Share of the regions of each pattern that are ... (%):")
display(typ.round(0))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 3.8), dpi=110)
t_ = list(GEO_TYPES)
w = 0.8 / (len(shown) + 1)
for j, p in enumerate(shown + ["all regions"]):
    small_p = p in SMALLP  # small group: dashed outline, hatched
    ax.bar(np.arange(len(t_)) + (j - len(shown) / 2) * w,
           typ.loc[p, t_].values,
           width=w * 0.92,
           color="white" if small_p else PCOLOR.get(p, "#b9b8b3"),
           edgecolor=PCOLOR[p] if small_p else None,
           hatch="////" if small_p else None,

           linewidth=1 if small_p else 0,
           label=plabel(p, typ.loc[p, 'regions']) if p != "all regions" else f"{p} ({typ.loc[p, 'regions']})")
ax.set_xticks(np.arange(len(t_)), t_)
style(ax,
      "Typical geography of the foreign season patterns, NUTS-2, 2023-2024",
      "% of the pattern's regions")

plt.show()
ms_ = pg[pg["Gini"] >= LOW]
X_ = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(ms_)), ms_[GEO_SH].to_numpy() / 100, ms_[["Capital"]].to_numpy(), np.log10(ms_[["Nights"]].to_numpy(float)),
                      pd.get_dummies(ms_["Country"], drop_first=True, dtype=float).to_numpy()])
b_s, se_s, p_s = (v[1:6] for v in ols(ms_["SpreadRatio"].to_numpy(), X_, ms_["Country"].to_numpy()))
print(
    f"Test: Does a factor go with a season split into two (winter + summer)? Spread ratio of foreign nights ({len(ms_)} regions with a clear season), all vs none of the residents (capital: capital vs other), within countries:"
)
display(
    pd.DataFrame({
        "difference": b_s,
        "± SE": se_s,
        "p": p_s
    }, index=FACTORS).round(3))

  • Winter + summer regions are mountain regions: 91% are predominantly inland-mountain, against 15% of all regions. The test confirms it: within countries, a fully inland-mountain region has a foreign spread ratio 0.21 lower (p = 0.005) - a season split into winter and summer - while no other factor is significant.
  • Winter-season regions are too few to show a type: Lapland, Sofia's capital region and the island of Martinique share the timing, not the geography.
  • Year-round regions are city regions: 38% have most residents in cities, against 17% of all regions, a quarter are capital regions (25% vs 12%), and few are coastal (13% vs 25%).
  • Summer-season regions are the broad majority and look much like Europe as a whole, slightly more coastal (30% vs 25%) and rural (16% vs 13%): coast and countryside make the summer stronger.

4. What would more foreign guests do?¶

↑ Contents

Foreign guests are more seasonal than domestic guests in most regions. What does that mean for the region's year as a whole? Would more foreign guests change its seasonality?

In [25]:
# Both guest groups usable in the same year: monthly nights per day, per year and averaged
DOM, FOR = NPD.xs("Domestic",
                  level="ResidenceCountry"), NPD.xs("Foreign",
                                                    level="ResidenceCountry")
ok = USABLE.xs("Domestic", level="ResidenceCountry") & USABLE.xs(
    "Foreign", level="ResidenceCountry").reindex(DOM.index, fill_value=False)
ok = ok[ok.index.get_level_values("NUTSCode").map(REG["NUTSLevel"]) == 2]
d_y, f_y = DOM.loc[ok[ok].index], FOR.loc[ok[ok].index]
d_avg, f_avg = d_y.groupby(level="NUTSCode").mean(), f_y.groupby(
    level="NUTSCode").mean()


def gini_corr(x, y):
    """Gini correlation of x with y: cov(x, rank of y) / cov(x, rank of x)."""
    rank = lambda v: np.argsort(np.argsort(v, kind="stable"), kind="stable"
                                ) + 1
    return np.cov(x, rank(y), bias=True)[0, 1] / np.cov(x, rank(x),
                                                        bias=True)[0, 1]


def decomposition(d, f):
    y = d + f
    S_F, G_F, G_D, G = f.sum() / y.sum(), gini(f), gini(d), gini(y)
    GC, GC_D = gini_corr(f, y), gini_corr(d, y)
    assert abs(G - ((1 - S_F) * GC_D * G_D +
                    S_F * GC * G_F)) < 1e-9  # the decomposition holds exactly
    return {
        "S_F": S_F,
        "G_F": G_F,
        "G_D": G_D,
        "G": G,
        "GiniCorrF": GC,
        "GiniCorrD": GC_D,
        "RME": S_F * (GC * G_F / G - 1)
    }


def timing_effect(d, f):
    return gini(d + f) - gini(d + f.sum() * d / d.sum())


fe = pd.DataFrame(
    [decomposition(d, f) for d, f in zip(d_avg.to_numpy(), f_avg.to_numpy())],
    index=d_avg.index)
fe["ShareNights"] = 100 * fe["S_F"]
fe = fe.join(reg[["Region", "Country", "PrcForeign", "ForeignGroup",
                  "Nights"]])
print(
    f"{len(fe)} NUTS-2 regions with both guest groups usable in the same year")

257 NUTS-2 regions with both guest groups usable in the same year

Does today's foreign timing sharpen or smooth the season?¶

Timing effect = the region's Gini minus its Gini if today's foreign guests came in the same months as domestic guests. Positive = foreign timing sharpens the season, negative = it smooths it. Beyond ±0.01 Gini points and with the same sign in 2023 and 2024 it counts as clear; otherwise No clear effect.

Effect per unit of foreign share = timing effect ÷ foreign share of nights: how different foreign timing is, apart from how many foreign guests there are.

In [26]:
FCLASS = ["Smooths", "No clear effect", "Sharpens"]
FCOLOR = {
    "Smooths": "#2a78d6",
    "No clear effect": "#b9b8b3",
    "Sharpens": "#eb6834"
}
DELTA = 0.01
eff_y = pd.Series(
    [timing_effect(d, f) for d, f in zip(d_y.to_numpy(), f_y.to_numpy())],
    index=d_y.index).unstack("Year")
fe["TimingEffect"] = pd.Series(
    [timing_effect(d, f) for d, f in zip(d_avg.to_numpy(), f_avg.to_numpy())],
    index=d_avg.index)
stable = (np.sign(eff_y[2023]) == np.sign(
    eff_y[2024])) | eff_y.isna().any(axis=1)
fe["ForeignTimingClass"] = pd.Categorical(
    np.select([(fe["TimingEffect"] > DELTA) & stable,
               (fe["TimingEffect"] < -DELTA) & stable],
              ["Sharpens", "Smooths"], "No clear effect"),
    categories=FCLASS)
fe["EffectPerShare"] = fe["TimingEffect"] / fe["S_F"]
print(
    f"Today's foreign timing: sharpens {(fe['ForeignTimingClass'] == 'Sharpens').sum()}, smooths {(fe['ForeignTimingClass'] == 'Smooths').sum()}, "
    f"no clear effect {(fe['ForeignTimingClass'] == 'No clear effect').sum()} regions; median effect {fe['TimingEffect'].median():+.3f} Gini points"
)

                                             (s == "Sharpens").mean()),

                                            (s == "Smooths").mean())).round(3))
print()

How much would 50% more foreign guests change the season?¶

Every month's foreign nights grow by 50% (today's foreign timing); domestic nights stay as they are. Thick light grey = all guests today; coloured = all guests after.

Change in the region's Gini with +50% foreign nights: median +0.3 points (0.01); under ±1 point in 75% of regions; largest -2.3 and +3.6
Median change by today's timing class (points): Sharpens +0.8, No clear effect +0.1, Smooths -0.6

The effect is tiny. Even with 50% more foreign nights in every month, the median region's Gini changes by +0.3 points (+0.003 on a scale that runs to 0.917); three quarters of regions move by less than one point and none by more than 3.6, so the curves before and after almost overlap. More foreign guests push the season a little further in the direction today's timing already does: sharper where it sharpens, flatter where it smooths.

Conclusions and limitations¶

↑ Contents

Conclusions¶

  1. Volumes. Europe records 3.1 billion nights a year in tourist accommodation, 47% of them by foreign guests. Both are concentrated: the largest 10% of regions hold 43% of all nights, and foreign nights cluster in a few island, coastal and Alpine regions.
  2. Intensity and density. Relative to residents, islands and mountains carry the heaviest load (over 100 nights per inhabitant on the Aegean and Ionian islands), almost entirely from foreign guests; relative to land, capitals and city regions lead.
  3. Season. Europe's tourist year is a summer, coastal, August phenomenon (Gini 0.24 for the 34 countries together; August 1.9 times an average day). Capitals are the least seasonal regions in most countries; 77 of 268 regions have no clear season at all. Season75 says the same in months and follows the Gini index almost exactly.
  4. Foreign vs domestic. Foreign demand is more seasonal than domestic demand in most regions (176 of 257) and countries (19 of 33). Croatia, Bulgaria, Greece and Albania have the most seasonal foreign demand; Serbia, Czechia, Romania and Poland the least. The gap is about the same for Europe as a whole and for the typical region (about 0.04 Gini points).
  5. One season or two. In the Alps and the Czech and Slovak mountains, foreign demand is split into a winter and a summer season: the Gini index shows how concentrated their demand is, but their off-season is two short gaps rather than one long closure (Austria 15th by Gini, 31st by S_R). Across regions, a larger inland-mountain share goes with a more split foreign season.
  6. Shapes. Foreign demand has one summer season in most regions, winter + summer seasons in the mountains and a winter season in three regions (Lapland, Sofia's region, Martinique; a small, unstable group). The patterns follow a simple timing rule (is Dec-Feb, Jul-Aug or both above an average day?); the shapes form a continuum around the summer shape rather than sharply separate groups. Summer seasons differ mainly in length, and foreign guests' summer is usually shorter than domestic guests'.
  7. What more foreign guests would do: very little. Today's foreign timing makes the season clearly sharper in 125 regions and clearly flatter in 49; in 83 it makes no clear difference. Even 50% more foreign nights in every month would move the median region's Gini by less than one point (+0.003).
  8. Geography of the patterns. Year-round foreign demand is typical of cities and capitals, winter + summer seasons of mountain regions; summer-season regions look like Europe as a whole.

Limitations¶

  • Two years only (2023–2024). No pre-COVID baseline at NUTS-2 and no long-run change; the average reduces, but does not remove, one-off events (Easter falls in April 2023 and March 2024).
  • Establishments only. Countries may exclude establishments with fewer than 10 (in small countries 20) bed places, so small private rentals, often very seasonal, are under-counted, unevenly across countries. Intensity and density count only rented accommodation, so they understate the real pressure.
  • Volume floor. Monthly series under 100,000 nights a year are left out of the seasonality measures, because their Gini is unstable from year to year. In both years: the foreign series of Dytiki Makedonia, Ceuta, Melilla, Molise, Opolskie and Sud-Vest Oltenia, and the domestic series of Svalbard and Liechtenstein. In one year only (the other year is used): the foreign series of Severozapaden, Świętokrzyskie and Svalbard, and the domestic series of Ceuta. Volumes, intensity and density still include them.
  • Gaps and flags. Utrecht, Zuid-Holland and Iceland have 2023 only; Martinique has no 2024 months for domestic or foreign guests. Guadeloupe, Guyane and Mayotte have no usable domestic and foreign monthly series (missing or confidential months). Corse and the overseas regions carry Eurostat's low-reliability flag; Albania's 2023 values are Eurostat estimates. Serbia has no published area (no density); Svalbard has no residents (no intensity).
  • Foreign guests are one group - the data have no countries of origin.
  • The marginal effect assumes more of today's foreign guests, growing by the same percentage in every month; new markets with other seasons are not covered. It is relative to the region's Gini, so in nearly flat regions a large RME is a small absolute change, and it is near 0 where foreign guests are almost all nights.
  • Geography shares describe residents, not where guests stay; climate, access, ski and beach supply and prices are not in the data.
  • Accounting comparisons and associations, not causal effects.

Appendix¶

↑ Contents

Which series are used?¶

A series (one region, one guest group, one year) is used when all 12 months are published, none is confidential (Eurostat flag C) and it has at least 100,000 nights a year: below that size the Gini of a series moves several times more from one year to the next (Stage 2, A1). The table lists every series that fails the rule and why, including series with no monthly values at all. Months flagged u (low reliability) are kept and marked LowReliability.

One usable year only (that year is used): Utrecht, Zuid-Holland and Iceland (2023 only published); Martinique (no 2024 months for domestic or foreign guests); foreign guests in Severozapaden (2023), Świętokrzyskie (2024) and Svalbard (2024), domestic guests in Ceuta (2023), where the other year is under 100,000 nights. For these regions the timing classes cannot check that the sign is the same in both years.

How are the foreign patterns made, and how reliable are they?¶

  1. A year with no clear season (Gini under 0.15) is Year-round: its shape is mostly noise.
  2. For the others only the shape is kept: each month's deviation from an average day (factor - 1), scaled to unit length.
  3. The foreign NUTS-2 profiles are grouped by Ward's hierarchical clustering; the number of groups (3-8) is the one with the best silhouette (how much closer each region is to its own group than to the next one: above 0.5 strong, 0.25-0.5 reasonable, below 0.25 weak).
  4. Each group is named from its average profile: Winter + summer seasons if both December-February and July-August are above average, Winter season if only the winter is, otherwise Summer season. Groups with the same name are merged, and a group of fewer than 5 regions is folded into the nearest pattern.
  5. Every profile - foreign, domestic, all guests - takes the pattern of the nearest group average.
  6. The winter + summer group is mixed: it also holds profiles whose own year is mainly a winter or mainly a summer season. Its members are re-named from their own profile with the rule of step 4. This keeps a Winter season pattern; it has fewer than 5 regions, so tables and charts mark it as a small group and draw it with a dashed line.

Summer seasons are not split into "short" and "long": the shapes form a continuum, and the length of the season is what Season75 measures.

How reliable. The clustering itself is weak (silhouette 0.25: the shapes form a continuum around one dominant summer shape), and the final labels are exactly what the naming rule gives on each region's own profile - in effect, a timing rule. Measured on these labels the silhouette is 0.58, but most of that comes from the one large summer group. Five regions lie close to the cut-offs (table below). The winter season group is fragile: 3 regions, silhouette 0.17, Martinique measured on 2023 only, and in Stage 2 (R2) winter-season profiles keep their pattern in 2023 and 2024 only half the time.

# The final labels equal the naming rule applied to each region's own profile; list the regions close to its cut-offs
own = FAC.loc[[(k, "Foreign") for k in fo.index[fo["Gini"] >= LOW]]]
w_, s_ = own[["December", "January",
              "February"]].mean(axis=1), own[["July", "August"]].mean(axis=1)
print("Same label as the naming rule on the region's own profile:", (own.apply(
    name_of,
    axis=1).to_numpy() == fo.loc[fo["Gini"] >= LOW,
                                 "SeasonPattern"].astype(str).to_numpy()
                                                                     ).all())
near = ((w_ - 1).abs() < 0.1) | ((w_ >= 1) & ((s_ - 1).abs() < 0.1))
print(
    "Borderline regions (Dec-Feb, or Jul-Aug where it decides, within 0.1 of an average day): the pattern could change with small data changes"
)
display(
    pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region":
            REG.loc[[k[0] for k in own.index[near]], "Region"].to_numpy(),
            "Dec-Feb":
            w_[near].to_numpy(),
            "Jul-Aug":
            s_[near].to_numpy(),
            "pattern":
            fo.loc[[k[0] for k in own.index[near]],
                   "SeasonPattern"].astype(str).to_numpy()
        },
        index=[k[0] for k in own.index[near]]).round(2))

Do the season count and the patterns agree?¶

Season count from the spread ratio: one season 0.9 or more; main + secondary season 0.6–0.9; two seasons under 0.6; no clear season when Gini is under 0.15.

Median spread ratio by pattern: Summer season 0.99, Winter + summer seasons 0.53, Winter season 0.82, Year-round 0.93

Year shape clustering and the S_R ÷ Gini ratio agree almost completely. One season regions all have the Summer season pattern, and year-round and no clear season are the same regions. Ten of the eleven two seasons regions have the winter + summer pattern; the exception is Région lémanique, whose winter is just under an average month (0.99), so its own profile counts as a summer season. Main + secondary season is the mixed group: summer regions with a small second season (e.g. Kärnten, Drenthe, Extremadura, Bolzano, Övre Norrland), the three winter season regions (Lapland, Sofia's region, Martinique) and Trento, the one weaker winter + summer region.

What is the marginal effect of more foreign guests (RME)?¶

The same question as the 50% scenario in Part 4, answered for a 1% increase. The main text uses the timing effect and the 50% scenario.

The region's Gini splits exactly into the contributions of domestic and foreign guests (Lerman & Yitzhaki 1985). For foreign guests: S_F (foreign share of the region's nights), G_F (Gini of foreign nights alone) and Γ_F (Gini correlation: how far foreign guests' busy months coincide with the region's).

Relative marginal effect RME = S_F × (Γ_F × G_F ÷ G − 1), where G is the region's Gini: the percentage change in the region's Gini when foreign nights grow by 1% in every month (more of today's foreign guests, with today's timing). Outcomes: Flatten - RME −0.02 or lower; Sharpen - +0.02 or higher; Little effect - in between, or the sign changes between 2023 and 2024 (Fernández-Morales, Cisneros-Martínez & McCabe 2016). The paper's split of flatten into "flatter" and "off-peak" demand is not stable in these data and is not used (Stage 2, R5).

In [33]:
OUT = ["Flatten", "Little effect", "Sharpen"]
OCOLOR = {
    "Flatten": "#2a78d6",
    "Little effect": "#b9b8b3",
    "Sharpen": "#eb6834"
}
rme_y = pd.Series([
    decomposition(d, f)["RME"] for d, f in zip(d_y.to_numpy(), f_y.to_numpy())
],
                  index=d_y.index).unstack("Year")
stable_rme = (np.sign(rme_y[2023]) == np.sign(
    rme_y[2024])) | rme_y.isna().any(axis=1)
fe["Outcome"] = pd.Categorical(np.select([(fe["RME"] <= -0.02) & stable_rme,
                                          (fe["RME"] >= 0.02) & stable_rme],
                                         ["Flatten", "Sharpen"],
                                         "Little effect"),
                               categories=OUT)
display(
    pd.DataFrame({
        "regions":
        fe["Outcome"].value_counts().reindex(OUT),
        "share of Europe's nights in these regions, %":
        (100 * fe.groupby("Outcome", observed=False)["Nights"].sum() /
         fe["Nights"].sum()).round(1),
        "median foreign share of nights, %":
        fe.groupby("Outcome", observed=False)["ShareNights"].median().round(0)
    }))
le = fe[fe["Outcome"] == "Little effect"]
why = pd.Series(np.select(
    [(~stable_rme).reindex(le.index) &
     (le["RME"].abs() >= 0.02), le["S_F"] >= 0.85, le["S_F"] < 0.2], [
         "sign changes between 2023 and 2024",
         "foreign guests are the season (85%+ of nights)",
         "few foreign guests (under 20% of nights)"
     ], "small effect, foreign share 20-85%"),
                index=le.index)
print("Why 'little effect': " +
      "; ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in why.value_counts().items()) +
      f" ({', '.join(le.loc[why.str.startswith('foreign'), 'Region'])})")
region_map(
    {k: OCOLOR[v]
     for k, v in fe["Outcome"].items()},
    [(f"{o} ({(fe['Outcome'] == o).sum()})", OCOLOR[o]) for o in OUT],
    "What would more foreign guests do to the regional season? 2023-2024",
    "More foreign guests would")
print()
cols = ["Region", "Country", "S_F", "G_D", "G_F", "G", "GiniCorrF", "RME"]
print("More foreign guests would flatten the season most:")
display(fe.nsmallest(8, "RME")[cols].round(3).reset_index(drop=True))
print("More foreign guests would sharpen the season most:")
display(fe.nlargest(8, "RME")[cols].round(3).reset_index(drop=True))
